title: Speculoos (Spiced Caramel Biscuits)
summary: Thin, spiced biscuits with a deep caramel flavour from dark brown sugar, rolled and chilled for clean edges and baked to a crisp, snappy finish.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cream butter and sugar
steps.text: Beat the butter and dark brown soft sugar on medium speed for 3-4 minutes, until lighter in colour and creamy, then beat in the milk. The dark brown sugar brings both a deep caramel flavour and some of the moisture that holds the dough together.

steps.title: Mix in dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the flour, cinnamon, ginger, cardamom, nutmeg, cloves, bicarbonate of soda and salt together, then add to the butter mixture on low speed until a firm dough forms. There's no egg in this dough, which is exactly what bakes into a crisp, snappy biscuit rather than a soft one.

steps.title: Roll and chill
steps.text: Roll the dough between two sheets of baking paper to 4mm thick, slide it onto a tray and chill for 1 hour until firm. Cold dough cuts cleanly and holds its sharp edges, while warm dough tends to smear at the cut lines.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Give the oven at least 20 minutes to reach 175°C (155°C fan) before baking. A fully heated oven helps the biscuits dry out evenly for that characteristic snap.

steps.title: Cut into shapes
steps.text: Cut the dough into 7 x 4cm rectangles and space them 2cm apart on the metal lined trays. Gather, re-roll and chill the scraps once to use up the dough without overworking it.

steps.title: Bake until darkened at the edges
steps.text: Bake one tray at a time for 12-15 minutes, until the biscuits are firm, dry on top and a shade darker at the edges. That slight darkening shows the sugars at the edge have caramelised, which is where much of the flavour comes from.

steps.title: Cool to crisp up
steps.text: Cool on the tray for 10 minutes, then move to a wire rack. They continue to crisp up as they cool, so they'll feel firmer once fully cold than they do straight from the oven.

tips: Chill the rolled dough properly before cutting - a common mistake is cutting it while still soft, which blurs the edges and makes the shapes spread unevenly in the oven.
Roll the dough to an even 4mm thickness throughout so all the biscuits bake in the same time.
Re-roll the scraps only once, as handling the dough too much makes the biscuits tougher rather than crisp.
Watch for the edges turning a shade darker rather than relying on time alone, since ovens vary.
Let them cool fully before storing - they're still a little soft warm and only reach their proper snap once cold.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 2 weeks; they tend to improve slightly after a day or two as the spices mellow. The unbaked dough can be frozen, well wrapped, for up to 2 months.
